ambiguities.text: The specification does not explicitly define what happens if the apply_dao() function is called multiple times
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume apply_dao() is idempotent or only called once at fork block. Moving zero balance has no effect on second call.

ambiguities.text: The term 'irregular state change' is used without formal definition of how it differs from regular state transitions
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume 'irregular' means: not triggered by transaction execution, bypasses normal EVM execution, manually modifies account balances.

implicit_assumptions.description: The list of 117 DAO_ACCOUNTS is assumed to be complete and correct, identifying all affected addresses
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Incomplete list could leave attacker-controlled funds unretrieved or incorrectly confiscate legitimate funds

implicit_assumptions.description: All nodes in the network must apply the same fork logic at the same block number for consensus
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Nodes disagreeing on fork application would cause chain split (as actually happened with Ethereum Classic)

implicit_assumptions.description: The recovery contract at 0xbf4ed7b27f1d666546e30d74d50d173d20bca754 is assumed to be secure and correctly distribute funds
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Buggy recovery contract could lock funds or allow unauthorized withdrawals

implicit_assumptions.description: The b'dao-hard-fork' extra data marker cannot be accidentally or maliciously included in non-fork blocks
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Marker presence in wrong blocks could confuse fork detection logic in some implementations
